title: Android still dominates global smartphone sales; Google’s Pixel 10a shines in one country
snippet: Updated data shows that, yep, Android is still the dominant force in the global smartphone market, but country-by-country breakdowns would hint otherwise – and Google’s Pixel series really only breaks into the conversation in one country, too. more…
fullText:
Updated data shows that, yep, Android is still the dominant force in the global smartphone market, but country-by-country breakdowns would hint otherwise – and Google’s Pixel series really only breaks into the conversation in one country, too.

Counterpoint Research published a breakdown of global smartphone OS share, measured by sales, with Android taking the win by a mile. On the global scale, Android makes up about 75% of smartphone sales compared to iOS, which makes up 20%. The last 5% is Huawei’s HarmonyOS. Q2 2026’s numbers aren’t that different from the same time last year, with Android down from 79%, ceding 4% to Apple and 1% to Huawei.

Counterpoint Research

The report brings out that the popularity of the Galaxy S26 series, the Ultra in particular, helped in “mitigating” Android’s overall decline amid RAMageddon’s impact on the market. 

Android’s sales share fell 4% YoY in Q2 2026 to 75%, as competition from iOS and HarmonyOS intensified. The Samsung Galaxy S26 series performed better than its predecessor, mitigating the overall decline in Android’s share. Chinese Android OEMs are shifting their focus to higher-value devices and scaling back activity in the entry-level segment to navigate RAM shortages and rising costs.

Meanwhile, another Counterpoint report breaks down the top five best-selling smartphones in major markets across the globe in Q2 2025, with most markets seeing Apple’s iPhone 17 series up on top. That includes, Japan, which stands out on the list because right behind the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17E is Google’s Pixel 10a, the only place Google stands out in all of this talk about top-selling phones. The Pixel 10a made up 7% of Japan’s smartphone sales in Q2, continuing a trend of popularity among Google’s budget-conscious Pixel in the region. It’s also noteworthy as the Pixel 9a didn’t make the same list this time last year.

title: They’re Putting Cameras In Dishwashers Now, and It Makes More Sense Than You’d Think
snippet: Miele’s new dishwasher integrates camera technology, hot air drying and automatic dosing. I got a sneak peek at IFA 2026.
fullText:
The dishwasher felt like the final frontier for cameras in the kitchen. Cams and sensors have found their way into most major appliances. Ovens have cameras that watch food as it cooks and alert you when it’s properly browned, and smart refrigerators will ping you when you’re running low on eggs and suggest recipes based on what’s lingering in the crisper. But I failed to see an obvious use for hidden cameras in dishwashers.

When I heard that Miele had snuck one into its new model, unveiled this week at IFA 2026 in Berlin, I was suspicious. After a brand rep walked me through the new Diamond G8 and its novel smart features, I began to see some appeal.

A camera in Miele’s new dishwasher helps it choose the perfect cycle.David Watsky/CNET

The small camera, fixed to the back of the dishwasher door, gets a clear shot of the dishwasher’s interior. It uses that view to take inventory of what’s inside, recognizing dozens of common kitchen items and tailoring the wash cycle and detergent volume accordingly.

The Diamond G8 is one of the smartest dishwashers we’ve encountered, and it’s easy on the eyes.

Got portable bottles or reusable straws in the dedicated slots? The dishwasher’s brain will recognize them and make sure those items get the spritz they need. Load it up with pots and pans and the camera identifies them, triggering a more intensive cycle so everything comes out clean. A smaller load prompts a lighter cycle, so you’re not wasting more hot water or soap than is needed.

The G8 recognizes straws, flatware, silverware and cookware and adjusts its cycle for optimized cleaning.

The camera also determines how full the dishwasher is. Command the G8 to start when it reaches, say, 80% capacity, and it’ll monitor the load and automatically begin a cycle once it hits that threshold. 

One of my favorite features has nothing to do with the camera

The G8 Diamond takes advantage of fluctuations in electricity prices throughout the day. Tell it to run when electricity is cheapest, and the dishwasher waits for those lower-cost hours before starting its cycle. It’s a small detail, but it points to where Miele – and kitchen appliances more broadly – seem to be headed: machines that don’t just perform a task, but figure out the best and most efficient way to do it.

The dishwasher can be programmed to run when energy costs are cheapest in your area.

Miele’s newly unveiled machine has other AI-powered features that encourage efficiency and performance.  The G8 features careful water and energy monitoring, trackable through Miele’s app. There’s also a smart detergent-dispensing system, first introduced by the brand in 2018, and a beefed-up hot-air drying system, which Miele says gets dishes bone-dry every time.

The camera paired with a smart detergent dispenser doles out just the right amount of soap. 

Miele plans to roll out the Diamond G8 in the European market later this year as it considers a North American strategy, according to a spokesperson. 

A retail price is still under wraps, but I expect it to land in the super-premium zone. For a top-performing dishwasher you can buy today, see our list of the best models in 2026.

fullText:
New Apple CEO John Ternus has just sent his first company-wide memo. In it, Ternus thanks Tim Cook and recognizes that Apple is “so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity.”

“We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal,” Ternus also says, in reference to Apple’s forthcoming “Surprise and shine” special event.

Read the full memo, obtained by 9to5Mac, below. 

Ternus also looks further ahead in message, teasing the “incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet.”

Here is the full memo from Ternus sent to Apple employees today. 

Team,

Today, on my first day as CEO, I just wanted to send a quick note to thank everyone for the warm wishes. I also want to extend my deep appreciation to Tim for sharing so much of his knowledge and experience during this transition, and more importantly, for everything he contributed to Apple over the years. We’re so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity. We are all better for it, and I’m so grateful he’ll be our executive chairman.

I’m honored to be stepping into this role at what is truly the greatest company in the world, and I am so excited about everything we have in store. We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal. Thanks for everything you’ve all done to make it possible.

I’m just as excited about what lies beyond that, including the incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet that we’ll dream up and create together. There’s no team in the world I’d rather build the future with.

More to come. In the meantime, thanks for your excellent work!

John

title: Dell’s new 14S laptop exists to challenge MacBook Neo and, somehow, might be even cheaper
snippet: Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper. more…
fullText:
Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper.

The Dell 14S is directly positioned as an “affordable” laptop for “students, college, and everyday life.” It features an aluminum build, 21 hours of battery life, and either an Intel Core Ultra 3 or Core Ultra 5 processor. The 16:10 display has 60Hz and 120Hz options while the hardware has two USB-C ports and an HDMI port, as well as a headphone jack. 

Dell says the 14S weighs in at around 2.5lbs and is just 13.5mm thick. 

In a Q&A on its blog, Dell directly positions the 14S as a “compelling” alternative to the MacBook Neo, though pricing hasn’t actually been announced at this point. The company hints, though, that it will be cheaper than the XPS 13 that already starts at $699 – in other words, Dell 14S might just be cheaper than the MacBook Neo.

	

The Dell 14S is available in the United States this fall. Pricing will be announced closer to availability in each market. What we can say is that the Dell 14S is designed to be complementary to XPS 13 and accessible for students and young adults globally. We’re committed to making sure regional pricing reflects that too.

Amusingly, Dell acknowledges that it already launched a laptop called the “14S” earlier this year, saying that the “old” one is designed for creators, while this “new” model “prioritizes everyday performance, long battery life, portability, colorful design and accessible pricing.” Perfectly not confusing.

title: Samsung’s latest Galaxy Book 6 starts at $799 with 8GB of RAM
snippet: Samsung is launching a new laptop in its Galaxy Book 6 series, and it’s much more affordable with a starting price of $799. more…
fullText:
Samsung is launching a new laptop in its Galaxy Book 6 series, and it’s much more affordable with a starting price of $799.

Announced this week, the latest Galaxy Book 6 release is a mid-tier version of Samsung’s laptop, cutting down on some key specs in order to hit a lower price point. Where the current lowest-priced option is a 14-inch (IPS) Galaxy Book 6 with 512GB of storage, 16GB of RAM, and an Intel Core Ultra 5 chip, the new model takes everything a step down with:

14-inch LCD display

Intel Core 3 or Core 5 processor

8GB or 16GB of RAM

256GB/512GB/1TB of storage

It’s a notable step down, but at considerable savings. Where that previously mentioned Book 6 starts at $1,249 in the US, this new release will start at $799 – $100 more than the MacBook Neo. 

The hardware measures in at 15.7mm thick, just shy of 3lbs, and has a 61.2Wh battery inside – Samsung claims 25 hours of battery life – with 45W USB-C charging. There are two USB-C ports, a USB-A port, an HDMI port, and a headphone/microphone jack. Samsung is also introducing a new “Violet Silver” color in addition to the usual grey.  It runs Windows 11 with Samsung’s usual suite of added apps that include a lot of integrations with Galaxy smartphones. 

	

Samsung’s new Galaxy Book 6 is available already in some markets, but not the US just yet. It’ll be available on Samsung.com and Amazon in the States starting October 5.

You can see the change reflected on the company’s newly-updated leadership page, with Ternus getting the CEO title and Cook moving to the Board of Directors section in his new role as Executive Chair.

Ternus’ rise to the top job is expected to herald a shift in company strategy, with a more product-oriented vision compared to Cook’s operational expertise. However, these changes take time to trickle down. His first public-facing role will be to introduce the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra lineup at the company’s fall media event, scheduled for September 9. 

Previously, the board of directors were listed on the leadership website by name only. Alongside Cook joining their ranks, Apple has expanded the section to include profile headshots as well.

title: Apple Watch Series 12: Three new features coming next week
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12.

#1: New S-class chip

Apple’s S-class chips don’t get meaningful updates very often. Even though Apple does change the number most years, actual CPU improvements are rare. And last year, the company skipped offering an S11 altogether and kept the S10 around.

But this year, rumors indicate an upgraded S-class chip is coming to Apple Watch Series 12. Likely named S12 or S11, it will be more powerful, faster, and also the first new Watch chip of the AI era.

Siri AI is a tentpole addition to watchOS 27, and it’s expected to run best on the new chip. But other everyday features should benefit from the new chip too.

#2: Always-on heart rate sensor and more health improvements

Apple Watch Series 12 has long been rumored to add new health features. For example, the FDA reportedly reviewed an upgrade to hypertension notifications that’s expected to debut next week.

One other specific rumor is that the heart rate sensor will get always-on support. This would match functionality offered by competing products like WHOOP.

Per Mark Gurman, the new Series 12 sensor can “continuously collect data throughout the day — not just when it senses you’re doing intense activity or at other random intervals.”

#3: Ceramic case option, likely in white and dark gray

Joining the usual new watch bands and case options, Apple is expected to debut a Ceramic case for the first time since 2019’s Series 5 model. 

Apple will reportedly offer Series 12 in two Ceramic colors: white and dark gray. Per Bloomberg: “Apple has tested both white and dark gray configurations for the Series 12 ceramic cases.”

It’s unclear how much of a premium Ceramic will add to the Series 12 price, but the last time it was offered, it started at $1,299—far more than Apple Watch Ultra costs today.

We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch.

On Tuesday afternoon, Pixel 11 series users received an OTA update to CD1A.260905.001.A1 (from CD1A.260714.001.A9). 

The Android security update level is “September 1, 2026.” (Note: Not September 5.) The install screen has the usual generic security message: “This update fixes critical bugs and improves the performance and stability of your device.”

So far, we have reports of an under 100 MB OTA hitting the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Google has yet to post factory or OTA images as of Tuesday afternoon.

	

This is not Android 17 QPR1. Several of the visual changes coming in that release are not yet present, so this is still the initial release of Android 17.

Rather, Google is likely rolling out this update as a hot patch for Pixel 11 issues discovered since last month’s launch. The fact Google did not wait for Android 17 QPR1 should be telling.

title: macOS 27 developer beta 8 now available, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Continuing Apple’s weekly test releases ahead of the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate, the company is now rolling out beta 8 for developers. Here’s what to expect. Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well. more…
fullText:
Continuing Apple’s weekly test releases ahead of the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate, the company is now rolling out beta 8 for developers. Here’s what to expect.

Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well.  

macOS 27 beta 8 now available

Developers can now install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 8, continuing Apple’s work towards the operating system’s official release in a few weeks.

While macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 didn’t include any notable user-facing changes, beta 6 introduced redesigned traffic light window controls with a more Liquid Glass-like appearance.

At this stage of the beta cycle, Apple appears to be increasingly focused on bug fixes, performance improvements, and other under-the-hood changes ahead of macOS 27’s public release.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces the new Siri app alongside Apple’s revamped Siri AI, as well as an AI-powered Shortcuts app that can create shortcuts from natural-language prompts. Safari also gains a prompt-based extension builder.

The update additionally includes new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring fixed-radius corners for windows and apps after macOS 26 introduced dynamically changing corner radii.

We’re digging through macOS 27 Golden beta 8 and will report back if we find anything new.

Installing the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here’s how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 8:

Back up your Mac

Open System Settings

Go to General ⇾ Software Update

Click the ‘i’ icon next to Beta Updates

From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta

Hit ‘Done’

Did you spot anything new in today’s macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google Maps has renamed ‘Lake America’ for users in the US
snippet: Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.” more…
fullText:
Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.”

If you are located within the United States, viewing “Lake Ontario” via Google Maps will now show the name “Lake America,” following last week’s executive order. 

Google, in a brief blog post, confirms that users in Canada will continue to see only “Lake Ontario” while users in other parts of the world will see “Lake Ontario (Lake America).” This can also be seen using a VPN.

From the United States
From Canada

Google continues to cite a policy in which it updates location names based on local government data; in this case, the US GNIS, where the name has been updated as of August 27 by the Department of the Interior following Trump’s order. Google referred to this same policy in February 2025 when it updated Maps to show “Gulf of America.”

	
	

Canada has confirmed that it will not be updating the name from “Lake Ontario,” with Prime Minister Mark Carney stating that “the name is more than 400 years ​old, predating ​both the Confederation of Canada ‌and ⁠the Declaration of Independence of the United States of ​America.” Carney added that the name comes “from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means ‘the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.'”

Notably, competitor MapQuest has directly said it will not change the name, instead building out a name generator that allows users to create their own new names for the lake, mocking the change. Apple Maps is not yet showing the name either. Apple changed “Gulf of America” within a day or two of Google back in February, though.

Steep backlash pushed Google to limit new reviews of “Gulf of America” in 2025, but the same limitation has yet to be placed on “Lake America,” we observed in testing.

title: AirPods 5: Here’s what rumors say will launch next week
snippet: Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods. more…
fullText:
Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods.

AirPods 5 expected to launch at September 9 event in two models, but no cameras

Apple’s biggest event of the year is happening next week on September 9. Alongside new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and likely Home products, AirPods 5 are also expected to debut. 

AirPods 4 launched in 2024, and historically Apple has had two- or three-year gaps between generations. AirPods launched in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. So from a timing standpoint, a launch this year more or less fits the pattern.

What’s surprising about the new AirPods, however, is how few rumors and leaks there have been about them.

Most AirPods rumors of late have centered on new models with cameras. A recent video leaked in Apple software showed the camera-equipped model in action, sparking speculation it would launch soon.

However, Mark Gurman at Bloomberg says AirPods with cameras will not arrive until 2027. But he’s expecting AirPods 5—without cameras—to debut at Apple’s September event. He recently wrote:

[Apple is] planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event. The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year.

In a post on X, Gurman added that AirPods 5 will come in two distinct models:

with Active Noise Cancellation

without ANC

Previously in his reporting, Gurman wrote that he doesn’t anticipate AirPods 5 getting the heart-rate sensor from AirPods Pro 3, but Apple “is looking to add several more health features to the AirPods over time, including a temperature reader.” He also noted separately that Apple is “working on an H3 chip designed for less lag time and better audio quality.”

It’s unclear whether AirPods 5 will get the H3 chip or not. When Apple launched H2, it was exclusive to the AirPods Pro line initially.

But new health sensors are possible for AirPods 5, and H3 is a possibility too. Otherwise, details on AirPods 5 are minimal at this point. Perhaps like it did with AirPods Max 2 earlier this year, Apple will be able to surprise us with its AirPods 5 reveal.

What features do you hope to see in Apple’s next AirPods? Let us know in the comments.

title: Oura files to go public
snippet: The ring maker says that its business has shown significant revenue growth over the past year.
fullText:
Oura, the smart ring maker, has filed to go public. 

The filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday shows that Oura’s revenue has jumped substantially in the past year. The company went from $697 million in revenue during the nine-month period that ended June 30 last year to $1.2 billion during the corresponding period this year.

The company has said previously that it generated $500 million in revenue in 2024, roughly $1 billion in 2025, and that it expected to generate close to $2 billion in revenue this year.

The company says it has sold 3.6 million rings over the past year, and that it currently has approximately 5 million paid members — that is, users who subscribe to its service for broader health metrics. The filing also says that Oura has an approximately 85% weighted-average 12-month membership retention rate, meaning that roughly 85% of members who sign up in a given month are still subscribed a year later.

The company’s rings, which sell in the range of $350 to $400, are, at their most fundamental level, fitness trackers designed to measure a user’s biometrics — everything from metabolism and heart rate to stress levels and sleep patterns. Paired with an app, the ring and that software are marketed by Oura as an “always-on health intelligence platform.” 

Late last month, it was reported that Oura was looking to raise $3 billion during its expected public offering. The company, which was founded in Finland in 2013, confidentially filed for an IPO in May. Bloomberg previously reported that the company is expected to seek a $16 billion valuation. In October of last year, it had been valued at around $11 billion.

In its SEC filing, Oura outlines where it believes its audience can widen in the coming years. “We believe our opportunity extends beyond traditional wearable use cases centered on activity and fitness tracking,” it says. “We believe our platform can support significantly larger populations as we continue to expand access, build clinical evidence, and deepen integrations with health plans, employers, and care providers.”

Oura also notes how its trove of data is fueling new AI integrations. “We believe we have amassed one of the largest and highest-quality longitudinal biometric datasets in consumer health, tracking over 50 health and wellness metrics and representing nearly 42 billion hours of physiological data,” it states. “This dataset powers our AI and machine-learning models, which decode complex physiological patterns and improve in accuracy, personalization, and predictive capability as member histories deepen.”

TechCrunch has reached out to Oura for more information.

The company, which now has offices throughout the world, including San Francisco, was recently hit with a proposed class action lawsuit accusing it of misleading users about the accuracy of its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit alleges Oura’s rings can’t actually detect the physiological signals needed to determine sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that the complaint describes as little more reliable than a coin flip. The litigation follows years of online complaints from users who said that Oura consistently rated their sleep as optimal when, in fact, it was not. 

The company has disputed the allegations and previously told TechCrunch it will “defend against” the claims in the “appropriate legal forum.”

title: ‘Look up’ app for Googlebooks appears on Play Store, currently works on phones
snippet: Following Magic Pointer and Desktop Camera, Google has now released a “Look up” app for Googlebooks. more…
fullText:
Following Magic Pointer and Desktop Camera, Google has now released a “Look up” app for Googlebooks. 

Look up lets you “highlight a concept you want to explore, a new word, a trip destination, and more.” This opens a floating window, with screenshots showing a dictionary, flight tracker, “Overview,” and translator. The “Ask a follow-up question” field at the bottom provides a conversational Gemini experience. The Play Store icon is a pair of glasses badged by the Gemini spark.

Google explains that “Look up will use publicly available information from the relevant Google service (e.g. Search, Maps, Flights) to provide the best response in a helpful format.”

The desktop interface and package name — com.google.android.desktop.contextualtools — make it clear that this is for Googlebooks, though the app can be installed on phones as of today. 

	

When you highlight text, “Look up” will appear as a menu option. This brings up the floating panel with results. Google will presumably close this unintended availability on phones in short order.

Look up is roughly analogous to a similarly named macOS feature (“Look Up”) when you right-click.

title: Android Auto 17.6 update rolling out with redesigned logo [Gallery]
snippet: Google is giving Android Auto a very slight refresh in its 17.6 update, with the app’s logo getting a new look that you’ll only see in a couple of locations. more…
fullText:
Google is giving Android Auto a very slight refresh in its 17.6 update, with the app’s logo getting a new look that you’ll only see in a couple of locations.

Related: Android Auto tests Quick Settings and hilarious ‘Jimothy’ weather Easter egg [Gallery]

In recent weeks, we’ve noticed a new green Android Auto icon showing up intermittently on certain devices, but it seems Google is ready to roll this one out to the wider Android ecosystem. With the Android Auto 17.6 update, a redesigned green icon has made its debut.

Artem Russakovskii of APKMirror noted the change, with the APK site also showing that this is the first version that fully moves over to the new look. Everything previously was using the older blue icon style.

Old vs New

Google also quietly updated the official Android Auto website with this new design, including on a video thumbnail advertising Gemini integration. We can also see the wordmark here, which is also updated from its previous look just a little bit. 

	

As far as the end user goes, the new Android Auto icon/logo won’t be visible in most cases. While we’ve noticed the green icon in some notifications, they’re mostly still showing a blue alternate icon. The only place you can consistently see it on Android is in the app switcher if you access Android Auto settings.

Notably, the Android Auto settings menu also now has a green accent color to match.

title: Lenovo Showcases Silent Ultraportable and Latest Rollable Laptop Concepts at IFA 2026
snippet: Project AeroBlade is an exciting new and fanless cooling system, while Project Swan builds on a motorized display concept shown off at CES.
fullText:
When it comes time for a big computing show, you can always count on Lenovo to exhibit some wacky proof-of-concept machines.

At CES 2026, for instance, the Chinese company debuted an AI-powered tracking webcam and a horizontal rollable gaming laptop display. Just this year, my personal favorite gaming handheld prototype debuted at Mobile World Congress, alongside a detachable dual-screen ThinkBook concept. Now, Lenovo’s coming out swinging again with its IFA 2026 exhibition – the company debuted two new concepts this time around in Berlin.

Project Swan is a 14-inch consumer laptop that can easily be toted around from place to place, before its horizontally rolling screen extends to 17 inches for work or entertainment. Project AeroBlade introduces a completely new ventless cooling system that minimizes noise pollution and supposedly doesn’t require any major compromises in compute performance.

If theoretical and fantastical concepts aren’t what you’re looking for, you’re boring and probably lack whimsy. But fret not, because Lenovo debuted plenty of products that it’ll be bringing to market over the course of the next 12 months, including a new type of OLED monitor, beefy (and expensive) desktop PCs and a handful of new consumer laptops.

The 14-inch design of Project Swan makes it ultraportable, but the screen extends to 17 inches when you need it for work sessions or entertainment.Josh Goldman/CNET

The Project Swan concept takes Lenovo’s rollable laptop screens in a new direction

Lenovo has never shied away from funky device displays. The company released or has shown off concepts for computers with vertical motorized rolling screens, laptop displays that wrap around the top lid to show off widgets while closed and screens that turn to keep you centered in the built-in webcam. At this year’s Mobile World Congress, Lenovo even showcased a prototype handheld gaming console with a folding screen that works in horizontal and vertical configurations.

The company is keeping the ball rolling at IFA with Project Swan, its first horizontally expanding, rollable work laptop. The 14-inch device can extend into a 17-inch display at the touch of a button. It’s a very large screen packed into one of the most portable clamshell designs possible.

The Legion Pro Rollable, shown off at CES 2026, uses much the same technology — but that was a gaming-centric laptop, tailored toward first-person shooters and other games that benefit from a wide field of view. I’m not sure how folks will respond to the deluge of laptops with rollable displays, but by my estimation, the Project Swan concept is one of the most practical Lenovo has shown off yet.

This seems like the starting point for a solid workhorse laptop: I can imagine using it for work and packing it away for trips, then unfurling the screen to use the computer for periods of high-productivity multitasking – or as a portable entertainment center for movies and shows. If this concept ever comes to fruition, it might be the most family-oriented rollable in Lenovo’s stable.

Lenovo’s experimental new ventless cooling system, AirJet, rests on Project AeroBlade’s chassis.Josh Goldman/CNET

The Project AeroBlade concept might save your legs from getting toasted

I don’t know about you, but I’m tired of singeing my legs when I push my laptop a little too hard and the vents dump all that excess heat right into my lap. I also hate when I’m bundled up under a blanket and the blocked fans start whirring concerningly loud.

Lenovo’s Project AeroBlade feels like the type of concept device that would tangibly improve just about any laptop user’s experience. This 14-inch ultraportable laptop has a new fanless design that Lenovo says won’t compromise performance. Instead, there’s a single vent running along the hinge, which allows outside air to pass through the internal thermals. And moving air through the laptop aren’t fans but tiny modules that use ultrasonic vibrations. Lenovo calls this vibrating cooling tech AirJet.

At a press event in New York, a member of Lenovo’s design team explained that the new cooling design is more akin to “a bike pump than a leaf blower.” Whereas the average laptop dumps heat in a single direction, Project AeroBlade pulls in cool air from its surroundings and circulates it through the inside of the laptop.

Whether or not this iteration of Project AeroBlade comes to fruition, it’ll be interesting to see if Lenovo’s new cooling solution ever makes it to the market. A cooler, quieter and higher-performance system feels like more than a marketing gimmick – if it works as advertised, this could seriously sway consumers toward a better type of laptop design.

Lenovo’s ThinkVision P27UL-40 monitor is the company’s first commercially available IJP OLED display.Lenovo/CNET

The ThinkVision P27UL-40 monitor is Lenovo’s first InkJet printing OLED display

If you’re looking for a best-in-class monitor, odds are good you’re looking for a display with an OLED panel – the quicker response time gives the tech an edge over IPS LCDs. But while OLED monitors have become significantly more affordable over the past decade, they’re still a bit too pricey for some folks.

Those prices may start to come down an appreciable amount again in the near future, thanks to new inkjet-printing OLED tech. These displays literally use a printer to deposit organic material on a glass layer thousands of times per second.

The result is a display that doesn’t compromise color contrast or picture quality, though it hasn’t achieved anywhere close to the same level of brightness as traditional OLEDs. Some analysts believe the IJP OLEDs might cut production costs by up to 20%, and some of those savings will be passed on to the consumer.

Lenovo isn’t the first to create a consumer IJP OLED screen, but the ThinkVision P27UL-40 is the first inkjet-printed monitor the company is bringing to the market. This 27-inch monitor has a 3,840×2,160-pixel resolution panel and an up to 120Hz refresh rate.

The ThinkVision P27UL-40 will be released in March 2027, starting at $1,300, which is still a significant chunk of change. But if industry analysts are right, this might be the start of a trend leading to more competitively priced OLED monitors.

Other ThinkVision monitors also debuted at IFA 2026, but none of those models use the same IJP OLED technology as the ThinkVision P27UL-40. Instead, they’re rather standard LCD monitors.

The ThinkVision T32WD-4v is a 32-inch IPS monitor with 3,840×2,160-pixel resolution and an up to 120Hz refresh rate. It’ll start shipping in February next year and start at $900. 

The ThinkVision T34WD-4v is the larger addition to the ThinkVision T series lineup: It’s a 34-inch VA monitor with 3,440×1,440-pixel resolution and an up-to-120Hz refresh rate. That monitor will start shipping in January with a starting price of $1,000.

Lenovo’s ThinkCentre X Ultra desktop has high compute performance with a price to match, but it’s packaged into the tiny form you see above.Lenovo/CNET

The ThinkCentre X Ultra desktop is a rather robust AI-first workhorse

If you’ve got enough pocket change to ignore the surging hardware costs spurred by the RAMageddon, maybe Lenovo’s new ThinkCentre X Ultra desktop PC is for you. This veritable powerhouse is an “AI-first” juggernaut, with a design crafted to optimize compute power (though a computer like this could realistically handle most tasks you throw at it).

This 4.4-pound computer is powered by AMD silicon, housing an up-to-Ryzen AI Max Plus Pro 495 processor. It features integrated graphics, up to 128GB of RAM and 8TB of system storage. There are two expansion slots for additional SSDs, assuming you have the cash for upgrades after buying this desktop. The ThinkCentre X Ultra will be released in November at a starting price of $3,700.

Alongside the ThinkCentre X Ultra, Lenovo is debuting two other desktop PCs. The 2.6-pound ThinkCentre M75q Gen 6 is even more compact than the Ultra, but still retains some beefy AMD processing power. This desktop is powered by up to Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450GE silicon, has integrated Radeon 860M graphics, up to 64GB of RAM and 4TB of storage space. The M75q Gen 6 will be available later this month at a starting price of $1,380.

The ThinkCentre M75s Gen 6, on the other hand, is the largest desktop PC in the new lineup. Weighing in at 10.6 pounds, this computer is powered by an up-to-Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450G processor, 64GB of RAM and 4TB of storage. Different configurations come with integrated Radeon 860M and Radeon RX 6400 8GB graphics. The M75s Gen 6 will be available next month at a starting price of $1,490.

I put my hands on the ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 at a press event in New York – it was an appreciably slim ultraportable clamshell design to refresh the lineup.Josh Goldman/CNET

Two new sleek and slim 14-inch ThinkBooks

Lenovo may not have debuted any wacky new ThinkBook concepts at IFA, but the company showed off two new 14-inch iterations of its popular work laptop lineup that will begin shipping soon.

The ThinkBook 14 Gen 9 is a balanced 2.8-pound laptop, packaging a decent 14-inch, 1,920×1,200-pixel resolution display and solid internal specs into a single clamshell. It’s powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus processor and a Qualcomm Adreno GPU, and has up to 32GB of LPDDR5x RAM and a 1TB SSD (with the option to slot in a second SSD). The ThinkBook 14 Gen 9 will be released next month with a starting price of $1,300.

The ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 is the sleek ultraportable offering, weighing just under 2.2 pounds. Lenovo packed some decent hardware into this clamshell despite its diminutive size, and the optional 2.8K OLED screen will provide snappy color contrast that’ll satisfy most folks.

The ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 is powered by Intel Core 7 Series 3 silicon, integrated graphics, up to 32GB of LPDDR5x memory and 2TB of storage space. It will be released in early 2027 and start at $1,000.

title: Android Auto tests Quick Settings and hilarious ‘Jimothy’ weather Easter egg [Gallery]
snippet: Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu. more…
fullText:
Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu.

About APK Insight: In this “APK Insight” post, we’ve decompiled the latest version of an application that Google uploaded to the Play Store. When we decompile these files (called APKs, in the case of Android apps), we’re able to see various lines of code within that hint at possible future features. Keep in mind that Google may or may not ever ship these features, and our interpretation of what they are may be imperfect. We’ll try to enable those that are closer to being finished, however, to show you how they’ll look in case that they do ship. With that in mind, read on.

In a teardown of Android Auto 17.6, we can see Google setting the stage for an implementation of Quick Settings tiles in the car UI. Strings currently point to a “Do Not Disturb” tile, but it lays the groundwork for future additions.

<string name=”quick_settings_tile_dnd”>Do Not Disturb</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_off”>Do Not Disturb turned off</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_on”>Do Not Disturb turned on</string>

This is not currently user-facing within Android Auto, but the folks over at Android Authority manually activated the feature, showing that it appears in the notification tray.

	

While this feels like a natural addition for Android Auto and like something Google would actually release to users, the other addition in Android Auto 17.6 feels like a fun little joke at best.

“Jimothy,” the viral raccoon, is hiding in Android Auto with a flag for a “Jimothy mode.”

SystemUi__jimothy_mode_enabled

Enabling this one shows “Jimothy” with weather animations, showing the current temperature and conditions on top of your music widget. It’s hilarious and very fun, but also incredibly unlikely to be something Google actually releases to the public – if nothing else, the meme’s time has passed. 

But, Google, this should absolutely happen with “Froggy,” as it’d be a fun and fitting way to finally show weather data consistently on Android Auto.

title: MacBook Neo 2: Here’s everything we know so far
snippet: Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop … more…
fullText:
Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop …

MacBook Neo 2 features

A19 Pro chip

The current MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip, which is the same chip used in the iPhone 16 Pro. As reported by Bloomberg, Apple is working on a next-generation MacBook Neo powered by the A19 Pro chip.

In terms of performance, the A19 Pro is about 10-15% faster than the A18 Pro in single-core and multi-core CPU tests. The jump in GPU performance is even bigger, with benchmarks showing an up to 40% boost for the A19 Pro. This is because every GPU core in the A19 Pro has Neural Accelerators built in.

The A19 Pro chip is also used in the flagship iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air.

According to reporter Tim Culpan, Apple will likely use a “binned” version of the A19 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo. While the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro has a 6-core GPU, the MacBook Neo version of the chip will likely have a 5-core GPU.

More memory

One of the compromises of the MacBook Neo is that it has 8GB of RAM. The rest of Apple’s Mac lineup nowadays starts with 16GB of RAM.

The next-generation MacBook Neo won’t jump all the way to 16GB of RAM. Instead, it’s expected to offer 12GB of RAM thanks to the aforementioned A19 Pro.

As I wrote in my review, I don’t think it’s a huge limitation that the MacBook Neo has just 8GB of RAM. Still, an increase for the next-generation model is a great improvement.

New AI features

The combination of the A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM upgrades should also unlock support for Apple’s more powerful on-device AI model announced at WWDC. This model enables a more accurate dictation experience and new options for customizing the Siri voice.

The current MacBook Neo doesn’t support this feature because of its A18 Pro chip and 8GB of RAM.

New colors

The MacBook Neo is available in an array of fun colors, including citrus, blush, indigo, and silver. Bloomberg reports that Apple’s plan is to “periodically” update the MacBook Neo with new colors.

There aren’t any details on which colors the next-generation MacBook Neo will be available in.

MacBook Neo 2: Release date and wrap up

Apple released the current MacBook Neo in March. Tim Culpan reports that the A19 Pro version of the machine is slated for a release sometime in 2027.

What changes do you want Apple to make with the second-generation MacBook Neo? Are you a MacBook Neo user? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Xbox Cloud Gaming will limit players to 15 hours per month before they have to pay more
snippet: Microsoft is making a change to Xbox Cloud Gaming that will place a limit of 15 hours a month or less on players before they have to pay more for cloud gaming. more…
fullText:
Microsoft is making a change to Xbox Cloud Gaming that will place a limit of 15 hours a month or less on players before they have to pay more for cloud gaming.

In a post today, Microsoft details that Xbox Game Pass subscribers will now be limited to a set number of hours per month, a restriction that does not exist today. Limits depend on the Game Pass subscription tier, ranging from 5-15 hours per month.

Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours

Game Pass Premium: 10 hours

Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Microsoft says that the change will impact “4% of Game Pass subscribers.”

Once someone uses up their allotted hours, more hours will be available for purchase through the Xbox Store. Pricing has not been announced, with more details to come in November when the change actually kicks in. Players will also be able to directly purchase cloud gaming hours even if they are not active Game Pass subscribers. 

	

Why the change? The company explains it is “because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer,” presumably all the more so in the midst of RAMageddon.

title: Apple Watch loses a useful multitasking feature in watchOS 27 that I’ve been missing
snippet: I mentioned today in my Siri AI Apple Watch piece that there’s one change I still hope Apple makes to watchOS 27 before it ships this month. It’s one of those common muscle-memory features that have existed for years, and I’ve been missing it all summer. more…
fullText:
I mentioned today in my Siri AI Apple Watch piece that there’s one change I still hope Apple makes to watchOS 27 before it ships this month. It’s one of those common muscle-memory features that have existed for years, and I’ve been missing it all summer.

Double-clicking Digital Crown no longer quickly switches between apps in watchOS 27

As I wrote this morning:

Now my one watchOS 27 complaint is that double-clicking the Digital Crown no longer jumps between recent apps… maybe watchOS 27.1 will do something with the double-click gesture. For a device so button-constrained that only the Ultra gets an Action button, it’s odd to see a double-click gesture replaced with … nothing.

I also flagged the issue in July when Apple released the first watchOS 27 public beta version, and I shared the feedback with Apple in June as well.

For years, Apple Watch has included a hidden gesture type of feature for quickly switching between two apps, or the last used app and the watch face. 

It’s one of those behaviors that I haven’t thought about in years, but I’ve used it regularly.

Dynamic app grid appears for Digital Crown single- and double-click in watchOS 27

watchOS 27 beta 1 dropped the feature. The reason seems to be that Apple is really promoting the new “dynamic app grid” feature in watchOS 27. Clicking the Digital Crown now shows the Siri app icon, plus five intelligently suggested app icons, and the icon to view the full app grid. 

The dynamic app grid has grown on me over time. It’s great if the app you’re looking for is already in the suggested launcher. 

But it’s not a replacement for a sure-fire behavior like double-clicking to jump between apps. There’s just no way to do this anymore with watchOS 27. Double-clicking the Digital Crown in watchOS 27 beta does the same thing as single-clicking the button.

The old method was super quick for jumping between apps like Workout and Music and the like.

As I mentioned before, the Apple Watch is so button-limited that only the Ultra model has the Action button. With this in mind, I think it’s a mistake to remove a double-click gesture from one of those buttons. 

Double-clicking the side button below the Digital Crown still has its assignment: opening cards in Apple Wallet. Hopefully the final version of watchOS 27 restores the same gesture for the Digital Crown button, or at least watchOS 27.1.

Do you use this gesture on your Apple Watch? Is it something you’ve missed in watchOS 27 beta? Will you miss it when you update? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live
snippet: Following the announcement at I/O 2026, Google is rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live this week. After testing in recent months, these voice capabilities are now generally available. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement at I/O 2026, Google is rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live this week. After testing in recent months, these voice capabilities are now generally available.

Gmail Live lets you talk to your inbox. Instead of manually searching for information and reading through threads, Gemini lets you have a “natural, spoken conversation with your inbox to pull precise information.”

You can ask follow-up questions without repeating the context, and Gmail Live can be interrupted at any time to switch topics without starting a new session. The fullscreen interface shows a transcript and links to the source emails. To launch, tap the new Live icon in the Gmail search bar.

Gmail Live is available with Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra on Android and iOS in English worldwide.

	

Google positions Docs Live as a “hands-free thought partner and co-writer” that helps you quickly create a first draft for summaries, proposals, and more. Gemini can draw from information in your Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web. 

It will show a recap of the information before proceeding to generate the document. You can ask Docs Live to add specific information and format as needed. In the Google Docs app, tapping the FAB (floating action button) reveals a new “Create with voice” option to launch the experience.

Docs Live is available with AI Pro and Ultra on Android and iOS.

Finally, Keep Live listens to “audio brain dumps and processes them” to generate notes and lists. Gemini “understands your stream of consciousness,” with Google Keep showing an inline preview of what it generated after a few seconds. 

You can tell Google Keep to put “ingredients for pesto pasta” in your shopping list, and “Gemini understands your intent and reflects it in the note.” Multiple notes can be generated in the same session, while you can use your voice to edit, like telling Keep Live to check off items.

Additionally, Keep Live isn’t limited to new notes and can add information to existing ones:

For example, if you already have a grocery list and you tell it you need to remember to get bananas, Keep will just add bananas to your existing list.

Keep Live is available on Android and requires AI Plus (updated), Pro, and Ultra. These three features are “coming soon” to Google Workspace business customers.

title: The XGIMI Aura 3 lineup brings Google TV to 4K 120Hz capable short-throw laser projectors
snippet: XGIMI has officially unveiled its new ultra-short-throw (UST) projector lineup at IFA 2026 with the debut of the Aura 3 Series, consisting of the AURA 3 Pro and Aura 3 Max. more…
fullText:
XGIMI has officially unveiled its new ultra-short-throw (UST) projector lineup at IFA 2026 with the debut of the Aura 3 Series, consisting of the AURA 3 Pro and Aura 3 Max. 

Positioned as the world’s first 4K UST projectors to offer 4K 120Hz output, the series targets both high-end home theater setups and high-refresh-rate gaming on massive displays.

Both models in the Aura 3 lineup feature an RGB Triple Laser light engine paired with XGIMI’s Dynamic Dual Iris optical system. The dual-iris system regulates light output to achieve a native contrast ratio of up to 8,000:1 alongside Dynamic Black Enhancement. 

The top-tier Aura 3 Max delivers up to insane 5,700 ISO lumens of brightness and covers 110% of the BT.2020 color gamut. With an ultra-short throw ratio of 0.163:1, the projector can project a 120-inch picture when placed roughly eight inches away from a wall, with supported screen sizes reaching up to 200 inches. That’s more than big enough for any home entertainment system no matter where you’re planning on making a home theater upgrade.

	

HDR standards supported across the lineup include Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG, and IMAX Enhanced, along with Filmmaker Mode, dynamic tone mapping, and Anti-Rainbow Effect (Anti-RBE) technology. The system also includes support for 3D content – yes 3D content in the big ’26 – and even ships with two pairs of 3D glasses.

To handle 4K resolution at 120Hz, XGIMI uses two DLPC 8545 display controllers operating in parallel. This is really good news for gamers because high-frame-rate gaming features are enabled via HDMI 2.1 inputs, including Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), AMD FreeSync Premium, and Dolby Vision Gaming, with claimed input latency dropping as low as 1ms depending on the mode.

On the software side, the Aura 3 Series runs Google TV out of the box and, unlike some options, provides native access to all the major streaming services such as Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube, as well as Google Cast integration. Audio is handled by an integrated 80-watt Harman Kardon speaker setup supporting Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X. When the projector is idle, an “XGIMI WALL” ambient feature allows it to display curated wallpapers and digital art.

Pre-orders for the AURA 3 Series are open now on XGIMI’s official store. Buyers can reserve a unit ahead of time with a $50 / £50 deposit to lock in an additional $200 discount.

One of the only frustrations is that the lineup will officially launch via Kickstarter on October 20, 2026. Kickstarter exclusive pricing starts at $2,199 for the Aura 3 Pro and $2,399 for the flagship Aura 3 Max. Not cheap, but certainly one of the most space-conscious ways to refresh your home entertainment setup.

title: Apple reveals ‘shocking evidence’ from ex-employee’s MacBook in OpenAI suit
snippet: Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu. more…
fullText:
Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu.

Apple first filed the lawsuit in July, accusing ex-employees of stealing trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI. It moved for a preliminary injunction a few weeks later, while also asking the court to expedite discovery, including early document production and depositions of key OpenAI employees and executives. Apple again emphasized the need for expedited discovery last week. OpenAI has called for dismissal. 

As covered before, Chang Liu is one of the parties named in Apple’s lawsuit. Liu was a senior system electrical engineer at Apple who left the company for OpenAI in January. The lawsuit alleges that Liu exploited a security bug to download confidential engineering files after leaving.

In today’s filing, Apple says that Liu’s lawyers recently handed over his MacBook that he used after leaving Apple. According to Apple, an “initial forensic analysis” of that MacBook revealed four things, quoted from Apple’s filing:

Mr. Liu not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work at OpenAI;

Far from his unauthorized access to Apple’s third-party cloud storage being unknown to him, Mr. Liu and others at OpenAI were well-aware of that access;

Mr. Liu, upon learning of Apple’s internal investigation of him, sent instructions for destroying evidence to an OpenAI colleague who confirmed she would comply; and

Mr. Liu used a tool in his work at OpenAI that has the same name as an internal Apple engineering application used for Apple development work.

Apple alleges that Liu ran a simulation in March using the circuit schematic file in LTspice, an electrical engineering tool. In messages from around that time, Liu said his AI “agent” learned to run LTspice and review the results.

Apple argues that when trade secret information is fed into an AI agent or model that learns from it, that learning “may create irreversible and continually propagating uses of the trade secret.”

Apple says the defendants decided not to inspect the laptop and instead chose to “advance theories that the device’s data disproves.” 

Additionally, Apple learned about Liu’s use of the schematic because he used it on a Mac mini which later synced via iCloud to the MacBook he took from Apple. Apple now also wants access to that Mac mini. 

This “shocking evidence” is yet another point in favor of expedited discovery in the case, Apple says:

“This shocking evidence—which Defendants chose to ignore despite its availability—demonstrates why Apple urgently needs expedited discovery. The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed.”

Earlier this month, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital said supply will be “extremely limited” at launch, but per his sources in the supply chain, there’s no evidence of a delay past September.

Similarly, a July report in Cailian News Agency referenced conversations with Apple supply chain sources. “They said that there was no change in the delivery time date in September, denying rumors of product postponement.” ChannelNews Australia was another recent source saying the device would be available in September, at least in the US.

Looking further back though, the story changes. 

Ming Chi-Kuo predicted earlier in the summer that iPhone Ultra will follow a similar strategy to the iPhone X in 2017. Meaning it could be announced in September but ship later in the fall. Macworld heard a similar plan from its sources.

And back in April, Nikkei Asia stirred a lot of buzz by reporting the foldable could be delayed several months into 2027. Mark Gurman at Bloomberg refuted that report though, saying the device was still “on track” for September.

iPhone Ultra release timing: wrap-up

In summary, the more recent reporting indicates that iPhone Ultra will indeed ship in September. It might be available in very limited territories and quantities, but early adopters should be able to buy it soon.

title: Leaker claims iPhone 18 Pro chip will have 7 GPU cores and faster RAM
snippet: A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models. These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … more…
fullText:
A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models.

These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … 

The images posted by Weibo user Fried White Rice are not of the A20 Pro chip itself, but rather diagrams of where the chip will be attached to the underlying circuit board. From this, they’re making inferences about the power and architecture of the new chip, drawing two main conclusions about likely improvements.

First, the diagrams point to six CPU cores in the same configuration as last year’s model: two high-performance ones and four efficiency cores. However, it appears that the cache memory for the efficiency cores has been increased.

We can see that the L2 cache for the small CPU cores has been increased—likely from 6 MB in the A19 Pro to 8 MB—while the L2 cache for the big CPU cores remains unchanged at 16 MB.

Trying to determine the number of GPU cores from the limited information provided by the solder diagrams is tricky, with six, seven and eight cores all possibilities. However, they conclude that seven cores is the most likely.

Again relying on the overall outline and solder‑ball positions, we can roughly deduce the GPU’s layout and explore several dozen configurations across three core counts—6, 7, and 8 cores. Ultimately, the 7‑core GPU configuration emerges as the most plausible arrangement.

Fixed Focus Digital recently suggested that the A20 Pro chip will be 18% faster than its predecessor with 30% better power efficiency.

9to5Mac’s Take

The Weibo account does have a certain amount of credibility, but this kind of indirect inference is very much a dark art. While the conclusions drawn are indeed plausible, they shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than informed guesses.

title: Google’s hyper-personalized ‘Dreambeans’ feed is now free to test
snippet: Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test. more…
fullText:
Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test.

Dreambeans is very much like a hyper-personalized Google Now or Discover feed. Like the Gemini app and AI Mode, it uses Google’s Personal Intelligence system to learn your interests by looking at your Gmail, Google Photos, Calendar, Workspace, Search history, and YouTube. During setup, you can choose which apps Dreambeans can access.

Workspace supplies ground-truth transaction data like receipts and upcoming flights

Photos provides the visual memories and insights about you and the people in your life

YouTube identifies your active hobbies

Search detects your budding interests

By combining all these unique signals, Dreambeans can proactively generate rich and highly customized daily visual stories.

The app suggests topics to explore, things to try, places to visit, and interesting events. New stories arrive every morning.

Instead of using stock imagery, each Dreambeans story is accompanied by Nano Banana 2-generated artwork that uses an illustrated style. For example, if Dreambeans recommends a hike, you might see yourself and a group of friends at that location.

	

Tapping on a story lets you see a longer description. In the same example, you’ll get trail details, specific places to stop, what to wear, and timing recommendations. Dreambeans will link to trail guide content on the web. There’s also an “Ask anything” chat experience to get more information.

You can leave feedback by tapping the heart or downvoting, while the chat interface allows you to provide more details. “Tune your feed” lets you tell Dreambeans what you “want more stories about” and what it should never show.

The name combines two ideas at the heart of the app. The “dream” is how the app works overnight to find meaning in the content overload across your connected apps. It then distills what it finds into “beans” – a fresh collection of stories brewed for you each morning.

In June, it was just available for Google AI Ultra subscribers, with Google expanding to AI Pro earlier this month. The setup process “requires up to a day to build your first set of stories.” 

It remains to be seen how Dreambeans will graduate from Google Labs. The experience it offers today is largely standalone, with Daily Brief in the Gemini app possibly benefiting from a more visual experience. 

Dreambeans is available on Android and iOS in the US.

title: Apple Maps still shows Lake Ontario as Google Maps changes name
snippet: The latest development in the trade war Trump started with Canada is an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Google Maps has updated the name, though what you see depends on which country you are in, with only US users seeing Lake America. Apple Maps has so far stuck to the real name … more…
fullText:
The latest development in the trade war Trump started with Canada is an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Google Maps has updated the name, though what you see depends on which country you are in, with only US users seeing Lake America. Apple Maps has so far stuck to the real name … 

Lake Ontario is this year’s rerun of the Gulf of Mexico. Trump last year signed an executive order stating that the latter would be renamed to Gulf of America, and has now signed another saying that the smallest of the Great Lakes will be renamed Lake America.

Canada and most of the rest of the world has responded with amusement and mockery. Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a new billboard on the shoreline of the lake reading “Lake Ontario. Now and always.”

Google Maps has updated its naming, with the label depending on where you are based:

US users: Lake America

Canadian users: Lake Ontario

Rest of the world: Lake Ontario (Lake America)

This mirrors the approach the company took with the Gulf of Mexico. Associated Press cites a Google blog post stating that its policy is to use the names assigned by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

So far, however, Apple Maps has stuck to Lake Ontario, including for US users. Whether it too will compromise as it did for the Gulf of Mexico remains to be seen. The company normally tries to avoid political flak, and has often taken the decision to appease the Trump administration, but with a new CEO, this may or may not change.

title: Apple reportedly considered launching a new Apple Pencil for iPhone Ultra
snippet: Apple’s first foldable iPhone should be making its debut in just over a week. In the development process, Apple was reportedly mulling the idea of launching a new Apple Pencil to use alongside the iPhone Ultra – though it probably won’t make it to market. more…
fullText:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone should be making its debut in just over a week. In the development process, Apple was reportedly mulling the idea of launching a new Apple Pencil to use alongside the iPhone Ultra – though it probably won’t make it to market.

This news comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who wants to make it very clear that this pencil probably won’t be announced next month. That said, he does detail exactly how it would’ve looked and worked.

It wouldn’t have been the same as Apple Pencils that currently exist for the iPad lineup. It was “stubbier,” to align with the shorter height of the iPhone Ultra. However, similar to Apple Pencils on the iPad, it would’ve magnetically attached to the side for storage and charging.

He notes that it would’ve been awkward to hold while you were using the iPhone Ultra, since it’d stick on the side, versus the iPad where it sticks at the top when you’re in landscape.

He also notes that it likely would’ve made “unsightly marks” on the much more delicate inside screen of the iPhone Ultra.

Ultimately, he reckons that Apple probably isn’t launching this to not conflict with Steve Jobs’ position when launching the original iPhone: “Who wants a stylus?”

I’d still say an Apple Pencil on iPhone Ultra would be rather useful, but it sounds like we won’t have one – at least for the time being.

title: Google Clock rolls out redesign of Timers with presets on Android
snippet: Following the new app icon, Google Clock has rolled out a redesigned Timers tab. This follows yesterday’s update to the Now Playing app. more…
fullText:
Following the new app icon, Google Clock has rolled out a redesigned Timers tab. This follows yesterday’s update to the Now Playing app.

The big change is that Google has introduced presets for 1, 5, 10, and 15 minutes that immediately start counting down once tapped. Google has tweaked the numbers at the top with Hours, Minutes, and Seconds replacing h, m, and s.

A big green “Start” pill replaces the previous icon at the bottom of the screen. Finally, the number pad no longer uses circular backgrounds. This tweak makes the screen feel flatter, with the interface now much busier but more efficient.

Old vs. new

	

If you have multiple timers, Google has shrunk down the cards and now offers a grid instead of the previous scrollable list. This is a much better use of screen real estate, while there are no changes to the single-timer look. The pause button is now inside the circular countdown, while reset is outside. 

This Timers redesign is rolling out as part of a server-side update with version 9.1 of Google Clock. If you’re not seeing it yet, Force stop from App info.

title: How to check if Motion Assist has rolled out to your Android 17 phone
snippet: Following the announcement on Tuesday, Google is slowly rolling out Motion Assist to phones running Android 17. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement on Tuesday, Google is slowly rolling out Motion Assist to phones running Android 17.

Once rolled out, you can search for “motion assist” in the Settings app. The long way is Settings app > Google > All services tab > Personal & device safety > Motion assist. Appearing alongside Advanced Protection and Theft protection, this new feature is part of Google Play services.

The preference menu lets you have Motion Assist automatically “Start in a moving vehicle,” but Google also recommends adding the Quick Settings Tile. This lets you manually enable and disable “from any screen.” You can add it from this page or the usual edit screen under “From system apps.” Once active, there’s also a system notification that lets you disable with a tap.

The Customize menu lets you adjust:

	

Color: Based on system, Red, Yellow, Green, Blue

Shape: Circle, Square, Pentagon, Diamond

Opacity: Slider

Randomization: “Color and shape change every few seconds”

The moving shapes adjust to the device’s motion and “may help reduce motion sickness when you’re in a moving vehicle.” On the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, you get three columns of shapes on the left and right edges, while Google’s phone example shows two.

Motion Assist is not yet widely rolled out. We’re seeing it with version 26.33.32 of Google Play services, but there’s a server-side component. As of today, it’s only appearing on one of our devices.

fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will have the same screen sizes as their predecessors, but rumors indicate their displays will be upgraded in two other ways. Here’s what’s coming.

#1: LTPO+ technology

LTPO is the technology that has long powered the iPhone’s Always-On and ProMotion display features. And in iPhone 18 Pro, Apple is rumored to be moving to the more advanced LTPO+.

Per The Elec:

Conventional LTPO applies oxide materials to switching thin-film transistors (TFTs). LTPO+ extends oxide usage to driving TFTs as well, enabling finer current control for OLED light emission and allowing displays to optimize operation based on surrounding conditions and user environments, improving battery efficiency.

Benefits of LTPO+ include reduced screen flickering in low-light environments thanks to more responsive adjustments, plus improved power efficiency. Thus, iPhone 18 Pro users should enjoy even more consistent display performance at a lower battery cost.

#2: Reduced Dynamic Island cutout

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s displays are also expected to have a reduced Dynamic Island cutout. Thus, the useable screen space will expand slightly.

The new Dynamic Island is rumored to be about 35% smaller than what iPhone 17 Pro offers. This size is even hinted at already by iOS 27 in Siri’s new design.

Apple debuted the Dynamic Island on iPhone 14 Pro back in 2022. While software features related to the Dynamic Island and Live Activities have expanded over time, the physical cutout has remained unchanged.

With iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple is finally moving a step closer to the dream of a cutout-free display.

What other changes do you hope to see in future iPhone displays? Let us know in the comments.

fullText:
CarPlay is about to get even better with iOS 27 in September. New features including a dedicated Siri app and Siri AI will upgrade Apple’s car infotainment system for iPhone users.

Even before the big iPhone software update officially launches, CarPlay in August has improved for everyone with three big app releases.

MLB iPhone app enhances CarPlay experience

First, MLB upgraded their iPhone app in the middle of the baseball season to improve the CarPlay experience.

Fans can browse live and upcoming games, select a matchup, and choose their preferred team’s radio feed. 

CarPlay also now shows baseball scores and key game details while the broadcast plays, with the app’s hide-scores setting respected for anyone avoiding spoilers.

Next, Meta AI for iPhone now works with CarPlay — with a catch.

The Meta AI app joins three other third-party chatbot apps that work with CarPlay: ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Grok.

However, Meta AI on CarPlay appears to be in limited testing for now.

Still, this shows the key benefit of CarPlay: integrating existing iPhone apps with your vehicle. You just can’t expect this amount of AI chatbot choice from built-in infotainment systems.

CarPlay adds a major weather app

The third big CarPlay app in August is Storm Radar from The Weather Channel.

Storm Radar for CarPlay includes a map of your location. You can toggle between satellite view and the default map background. Data layers include radar, clouds, and precipitation. 

Navigation is also a core part of the CarPlay app. Storm Radar displays your current weather conditions alongside the ETA and weather conditions expected at your destination.

The Weather Channel adds that CarPlay support includes “automatic rerouting and weather alerts along your route that refresh as you drive.”

More CarPlay upgrades

Looking ahead, Apple will upgrade CarPlay for everyone with the upcoming iOS 27 iPhone update. Installing the iPhone software update or upgrading to a new iPhone running iOS 27 when it comes out will automatically add new features to CarPlay.

In the meantime, Volvo has upgraded three SUVs with Spatial Audio through CarPlay for Apple Music and Apple Podcasts. This brings Dolby Atmos sound support to drivers. Earlier this year, Pioneer released an aftermarket head unit that similarly drives Dolby Atmos and Spatial Audio through CarPlay.

title: Belkin just released four Android Find Hub trackers; one is a full wallet
snippet: More companies are getting on board with trackers that work with the Android Find Hub network, and Belkin is the latest with four different designs. more…
fullText:
More companies are getting on board with trackers that work with the Android Find Hub network, and Belkin is the latest with four different designs.

Trackers come in all shapes and sizes, as long as the size is small and the shape is circular or rectangular. Belkin is mostly sticking to that unwritten rule with several entries in its new SureFind lineup starting at $15.

The smallest and most familiar tracker is the SureFind Spot. It’s the cheapest of the bunch at $15, and it looks a lot like an Apple AirTag, with a keyring included. The SureFind Loop Cable Tag is similar, but the fabric loop doubles as a spare USB-C cable. It’s a little more robust than the Spot, but it fits a similar profile for bags or everyday carry items that don’t require a compact solution. It also charges via USB-C, so it doesn’t need a coin-cell replacement every so often. The SureFind Loop Cable Tag will cost $24.99.

Belkin also released a card-shaped Android Find Hub tracker. Just like other tracker cards, the SureFind Card fits into most wallets and takes up no more space than a credit card. Its ultra-thin profile opens it up to other hiding places, as well. Belkin’s tracker card is IP68 for water and dust-resistance, too. It’s priced in the same area as the Loop Tag, at $26.99.

	

Of all the trackers Belkin announced, the last one is the most unique. We’ve seen the form-factor before, but it’s a welcome one. You could opt to slide a tracking card into your wallet, or you could skip that step and buy a wallet that connects to Google’s Find Hub network (and Apple’s Find My, though not at the same time).

Belkin’s SureFind Wallet Stand shows up in your Find Hub app like every other tracker, but it can’t be easily removed if someone were to take it. It doubles as a magnetic phone stand and comes in a thin compact profile that allows you to store a couple of cards. It’s the most expensive tracker Belkin released at IFA, coming in at $39.99.

Belkin says the SureFind Spot, Loop Cable Tag, and Card will be available starting this month from Amazon and its online store. The SureFind Wallet Stand will go on sale at the beginning of October.
