title: How to run Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering, high frame rate, and HD textures on iPhone [Video]
snippet: Love Mario Kart 64 and want to play it on iPhone? You may have tried Delta or another N64 emulator in the past to make that happen. And while that works, it’s now possible to run the classic cart racer with native Metal rendering on iPhone. As we’ll discuss in this video and post, running Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering presents several key advantages over running the same game via an emulator. Combined with a Bluetooth controller like the Mocagen MC1, it’s the best way to play Nintendo’s classic cart racer on iPhone. more…
fullText:
Love Mario Kart 64 and want to play it on iPhone? You may have tried Delta or another N64 emulator in the past to make that happen. And while that works, it’s now possible to run the classic cart racer with native Metal rendering on iPhone. 

As we’ll discuss in this video and post, running Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering presents several key advantages over running the same game via an emulator. Combined with a Bluetooth controller like the Mocagen MC1, it’s the best way to play Nintendo’s classic cart racer on iPhone. 

Native vs emulation?

Libultraship is a library that provides a reimplementation of the original N64 SDK on today’s hardware. SpaghettiKart is a PC source port of the original decompiled Mario Kart 64 cartridge that leverages that library. Developer Chris Sotraidis then repackaged SpaghettiCart as a native iPhone app called SpaghettiPad that features native Metal rendering, Bluetooth controller support, enhanced visual capabilities, and more.

Video tutorial

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

While it’s easier to get Mario Kart 64 running on iPhone via an emulator like Delta, running Mario Kart 64 natively on iPhone via SpaghettiPad provides a wide screen aspect ratio, frame rates up to 120 fps, higher resolution textures, better fps performance overall, plus lots of additional settings that aren’t available via emulation. And while SpaghettiPad isn’t devoid of glitches, I’ve noticed way less issues when compared to emulation.

One good example is Luigi Raceway, which features a jumbotron that mirrors your race activity. On the emulated version, the jumbotron is a choppy low frame rate mess, while it runs at a significantly higher locked-in fps on the native version. There a lots of little examples like this that I’ve noticed throughout my hands-on time.

Disclaimer: I own the original Mario Kart 64 cartridge. If you own the cartridge, you can dump the required ROM file. We will not be covering how to do that or how to download any ROMs.

How to run Mario Kart 64 natively on iPhone

Install iloader

Although iloader can be used to sideload an .ipa directly to your iPhone, the primary reason to use iloader for this tutorial is to use it as a way to facilitate the installation of SideStore. Beware of fake websites that try to charge money for this free open source software, you can visit the official website for iloader at iloader.app.

Step 1: Download iloader via GitHub.

Step 2: Mount the iloader.dmg and drag the iloader app to your Applications folder.

Step 3: Launch iloader and connect your iPhone to your Mac via USB. If prompted to trust the computer, do so and enter your device passcode.

Step 4: Click refresh under Device s, and you should see your iPhone listed.

Step 5: Enter your Apple ID Email and Password, and click Login. This Apple ID does not have to be associated with the account on your iPhone, and you do not have to be registered as an Apple Developer to do this. If you have two-factor authentication enabled, you’ll need to provide the authentication code that you receive from Apple.

Install SideStore

SideStore is an AltStore fork that lets you add repos, install .ipas, and signs and resigns those applications in the background to keep Apple’s 7-day development period from expiring. SideStore works in concert with LocalDevVPN to allow for truly wireless and Mac-free side-loaded app management.

Every app that you install with SideStore needs to register an App ID with Apple, and Apple limits non-developer logins to just 10 App IDs per week. After one week, these App IDs roll off. 

Apps installed via Side Store with non-developer logins are also limited to just three apps at once, and SideStore itself counts as one of those apps. 

Each app signing will expire after seven days, and you can refresh manually at any time. However, SideStore will automatically refresh apps in the background when connected to LocalDevVPN, and will re-register App IDs for installed apps automatically, no computer required. 

Step 6: Open iloader on your connected Mac, and click SideStore (Stable) under the Installers sections to install SideStore on your iPhone.

Step 7: On iPhone go to Settings → General → VPN & Device Management and tap the panel under Developer App that says “Not Trusted.” On the next page, tap Trust → Allow. 

Step 8: Open the SideStore on your iPhone, and you can select Don’t Allow on the network permission pop-up if desired, but you should choose to allow the notifications permission.

Install LocalDevVPN

LocalDevVPN is a free App Store app that serve as a loopback VPN that creates a virtual interface pointing back to your iPhone. It tricks iOS into thinking a paired Mac is attached to your iPhone, which provides the debug toolset that lets you install and refresh side loaded apps.

Step 9: On your iPhone go to the App Store and install LocalDevVPN. 

Step 10: Open LocalDevVPN, skip the welcome screen and click Connect → Allow. Enter your iPhone’s passcode to add a VPN configuration. The current status for LocalDevVPN should show Connected.

Install SpaghettiPad.ipa

Step 11: Download the SpaghettiPad.ipa from GitHub on your iPhone and save it to your iPhone’s download folder.

Step 12: Open SideStore, tap the My Apps tab at the bottom.

Step 13: From the My Apps tab, tap the + button in the upper left hand corner, and it will open the Files app interface. Select the SpaghettiPad.ipa and you will be prompted to sign in with your Apple ID on SideStore. You can use the same login/pass that you used for iloader.

Step 14: You should now see SpaghettiPad on your iPhone’s Home Screen.

Configure SpaghettiPad

Disclaimer: I own the original Mario Kart 64 cartridge. If you own the cartridge, you can dump the required ROM file. We will not be covering how to do that or how to download any ROMs.

Step 15: Via the files app, move the Mario Kart 64 (USA).z64 rom to On My iPhone → SpaghettiPad. 

Step 16: Open SpaghettiPad on iPhone, and tap Rescan on the “Add your game” pop-up. The next popup should say “Found Mario Kart 64 (US).” Tap the OK button to continue. You should see a black screen for a while, and then the “libultraship” splash screen will be displayed followed by the Mario Kart 64 title screen.

Step 17: Download the Mario Kart 64 HD texture pack and save the .o2r file to On My iPhone → SpaghettiPad → mods.

Step 18: Open SpaghettiPad and tap the ellipses button to open settings. Tap Enhancements → Texture Packs → Check Again. You should see a pop-up that says Texture pack detected. Tap OK. Tap the power button in the upper-right hand corner to quit SpaghettiPad, and the reopen SpaghettiPad to load the texture pack. 

Disable the libultraship splash screen

Step 19: Open SpaghettiPad settings again, and tap General. Under Startup Behavior, select Authentic. Now when you open SpaghettiPad, it will skip the libultraship splash screen. 

Enable higher Mario Kart 64 frame rates

Step 20: Open SpaghettiPad settings once more, and tap Graphics. Tap 60 FPS to jump directly to 60 FPS frame rate. If your device supports ProMotion, you can even select 120 FPS.

Connect a controller

There are many USB and Bluetooth controller options for gaming on the iPhone, including Nintendo’s own Switch Pro controllers, but I’ve really been enjoying the budget-friendly Mocagen MC1. It’s a spring-loaded controller that allows you to mount your iPhone inside and connect via Bluetooth. It features Hall effect analog sticks, USB-C charging, rumble support, dual triggers, RGB lighting, and more. In my hands-on experience it works very well with Mario Kart 64 on iPhone, and it features good build quality for the price.

9to5Mac’s Take

Emulating Mario Kart 64 via an app like Delta might be easier, but it doesn’t take that much effort to get SpaghettiPad running on an iPhone, and it provides a much better experience. SpaghettiPad provides full screen gameplay, higher resolution textures, and much higher frame rates than the emulated version of Mario Kart 64. If you’re looking for the best way to play this classic title on the go, this is the best way to do so.

What do you think? Sound off in the comments!

title: MagSafe Monday: Anker’s foldable 3-in-1 charger brings 25-watt Qi2 charging into something pocket-sized
snippet: The dream for your Apple gear while traveling is one thing, not a collection of cables and wall adapters. There are plenty of options for that, but often they are bulky. Anker’s Prime Qi2 25W Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger aims to address that. It folds flat, weighs about as much as an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods. more…
fullText:
The dream for your Apple gear while traveling is one thing, not a collection of cables and wall adapters. There are plenty of options for that, but often they are bulky. Anker’s Prime Qi2 25W Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger aims to address that. It folds flat, weighs about as much as an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

A 3-in-1 that folds flat

The whole pitch for this product is right in the name: it’s palm-sized and folds flat to fit in a pocket, bag, or travel crossbody, so it doesn’t take up much space. I’ve packed plenty of MagSafe stands for trips before, and they almost always end up being the bulkiest thing in my laptop bag.

Qi2 25-watt speeds

This is Qi2.2 certified, so you’re getting up to 25 watts of MagSafe charging rather than the old 7.5W ceiling that most MagSafe accessories were stuck at for years. Anker says it can get an iPhone 17 Pro to 50% in 26 minutes, up to 5 times faster than a standard 5-watt wireless charger. Your results will vary depending on the iPhone and its temperature, but even landing somewhere in that neighborhood is plenty.

Faster MagSafe charging usually means more heat, so Anker built in what they call AirCool temperature control. It runs at 19 dB, which is quiet enough you won’t hear it working, and it’s designed to keep your phone under 98.6°F while still delivering full 25-watt charging. Heat is the enemy of long-term battery health and charging speeds, so if this actually holds up to that claim in daily use, it’s a meaningful feature, not just a marketing bullet point.

The 3-in-1 layout covers your iPhone on the main MagSafe puck, an MFi-certified Apple Watch charger on the side, and a charging pad at the base for your AirPods. That’s the whole value proposition of a station like this: one cable to a power outlet instead of three separate chargers and three separate cables crammed into a bag. Here’s what Anker includes in the box:

Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station

45-watt USB-C wall plug

5 ft USB-C to USB-C cable

I love that Anker includes the wall adapter in the box, which matters since many chargers in this category assume you already own a fast enough brick. It also supports 110V to 220V input, so it’s a great item  for international trips without needing a separate voltage converter. 

Wrap up

Anker has made plenty of 3-in-1 chargers over the years, but the folding design is what makes this one stand out amongst a crowded market. It solves the actual reason most people leave their charging stand at home when they travel: they just don’t pack well. This one does.

You can buy the Anker Prime Qi2 25-watt Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger from Amazon or directly from Anker.

title: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 rolling out with many Pixel bug fixes
snippet: Following the big release two weeks ago, Google is rolling out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 for Pixel devices. As of Friday afternoon, the Pixel 11 series is not yet compatible, but Google says support is coming “soon.” more…
fullText:
Following the big release two weeks ago, Google is rolling out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 for Pixel devices. As of Friday afternoon, the Pixel 11 series is not yet compatible, but Google says support is coming “soon.”

Here’s everything new in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 [Gallery]

Android 17 QPR2 adds Status bar customization for notification, system icons

With Beta 4, Android 17 QPR2 has reached Platform Stability. This build addresses the following issues:

	

Enabling the “render apps below the cutout area” developer setting caused a transparent status bar on the launcher after exiting fullscreen video playback. (Issue #295747911)

A thermal management issue that caused devices to overheat and unexpectedly reboot during use. (Issue #437116407)

An issue preventing screen mirroring to external USB-C XR glasses. (Issue #439269938)

Gesture navigation became unresponsive when rendering apps below the display cutout. (Issue #441378954)

The 80% battery limit optimization caused excessive charge times during the final 2% threshold. (Issue #477009501, Issue #476803337)

A launcher UI issue where searching for apps in the app drawer failed to process text input. (Issue #505157934, Issue #527921034, Issue #530531588, Issue #537704656)

Invoking the power menu via hardware buttons caused a missing background blur effect behind the navigation bar. (Issue #537202501)

An issue where phone call audio defaulted to the phone speaker instead of connected Bluetooth devices. (Issue #537908014, Issue #541501134, Issue #541772860, Issue #545047074)

A Recents app switcher rendering bug where the first task card could intermittently freeze and visually clip behind other apps during horizontal scrolling. (Issue #530484511, Issue #505564040, Issue #545574713, Issue #551022006)

An audio service resource lock triggered during screen recording that prevented microphone usage across apps and input methods like Gboard and Gemini until a device restart. (Issue #538229807)

A System UI visual inconsistency where turning off the screen from the home screen triggered a plain fade instead of the power-button screen-off animation. (Issue #541261786)

A low-contrast rendering issue in dark mode where the connected Wi-Fi settings cog icon was barely visible. (Issue #536320341)

Enabling 3D mode on connected smart glasses resulted in a blank screen. (Issue #536628506)

A User Interface issue that prevented the notification bar from being pulled all the way down. (Issue #539244095, Issue #547801203, Issue #547017781, Issue #546896889, Issue #547163658, Issue #547281675)

An issue where WebGL applications could freeze or crash the browser process when combining shadow maps with vertex color attributes by resolving an invalid memory read in the PowerVR GPU driver’s texture state processing. (Issue #541322087)

Low-light Face Unlock failures bypassed Fingerprint Unlock and forced PIN entry. (Issue #547597971, Issue #545329611, Issue #541723970)

As always, you can report issues via the Android Beta Feedback app on Pixel devices. Access it from the application drawer or Quick Settings to file bugs in Google’s issue tracker. There’s also the Android Beta community on Reddit.

title: Read Tim Cook’s full memo to Apple employees on his last day as CEO
snippet: Today is Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO, with John Ternus set to take over tomorrow. To mark his last day in the role, Cook penned an emotional memo to Apple employees today. Read it below. more…
fullText:
Today is Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO, with John Ternus set to take over tomorrow. To mark his last day in the role, Cook penned an emotional memo to Apple employees today. Read it below. 

In the memo sent to employees this morning and obtained by 9to5Mac, Cook reflects on his time at Apple and thanks employees for all of their work. He also says he takes “enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable” as John Ternus. 

“Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership,” Cook writes. 

Here is the memo in full: 

Team, 

Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words. I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn’t let this day pass without sending a note to you, to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you’ve sent my way, for the way you’ve shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader. 

The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that. 

There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here. It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day. Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that’s the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our “dent in the universe,” as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world. How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am. 

As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership. 

I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make. 

I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world. 

With all I have and all I am, I am always 

Yours, 

Tim 

Cook also thanked the Apple community in a post on social media, writing: 

Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO. My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will. Thank you for being a constant source of inspiration. My gratitude is endless, and I’m excited for the next chapter!

title: From Folding Phones to Camera-Equipped AirPods, Here’s What’s Rumored for Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ Fall Event
snippet: Next week, Apple is expected to debut the Apple Watch 12 and new AirPods, as well as three new iPhones — but no base iPhone 18.
fullText:
After months of leaks and rumors, Apple is set to reveal its fall hardware lineup on Wednesday, Sept. 9, at its “Surprise and Shine” event. And from everything we know so far, the event will be unlike most others.

For one, this year’s event is a bit sentimental for the Cupertino company. Tim Cook announced in April that he is stepping down from his role as CEO, a job he has held for nearly 15 years after legendary Apple co-founder Steve Jobs stepped down in 2011. John Ternus, the company’s hardware engineering chief, stepped into the role just days before the event. 

Apple is also heavily rumored to break with its usual routine by holding off on releasing a base iPhone 18 until next year, meaning only the more expensive Pro models will be revealed in September. That would give another highly anticipated release center stage: the foldable device expected to be called the iPhone Ultra.

	

			

We’ll be keeping a close eye on the price tags. Apple raised prices across its computer and home devices this summer, attributing the cost increases to memory chip supply chain issues, largely driven by the AI race. Additional price hikes on Apple Music and Apple TV subscriptions aren’t helping cash-strapped consumers, either.

Read more: Win a New Apple Watch as CNET Guessing Game: Apple Edition Returns for Round 3

New iPhone 18 models, joining the foldable fun

Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup is likely going to look a little different this year. One of the biggest rumors is that Apple is going to do an extended rollout. This September, we expect to see the foldable iPhone Ultra, the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, but we likely won’t get the base iPhone 18, iPhone 18E and a possible iPhone Air 2 until spring 2027.

The iPhone Ultra, as Apple’s much-rumored first foldable phone is tentatively named, has a book-style design, according to analyst leaks. Think more Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which opens like a book into a mini tablet — not like an OG 90s flip phone. 

But the possible $2,000 price tag means the Ultra likely won’t be a replacement for the base iPhone 18. More likely, it will be more of a luxury option. That may be one reason why a majority of US adults (75%) don’t care about foldable phones, a recent CNET survey found.

We had CNET’s creative director show us what we could expect from the new potential iPhone 18 colors. 

Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max models are rumored to have bigger batteries, variable-aperture cameras and run on the new Apple A20 processor. More satellite connectivity, a smaller Dynamic Island and tweaked back camera islands are also possibilities. And these new phones could come in colors such as light blue, dark cherry and dark gray.

Running on all these devices is the already announced new family of operating systems. iOS 27, with the anticipated Siri AI revamp, is likely to be released this fall, along with MacOS Golden Gate, Apple TVOS 27 and more. Since we learned about these at WWDC in June, we’ve been playing around with the public betas to see what’s inside.

Apple Watch Series 12: Apple Health and Touch ID?

A Series 12 Watch is “all but guaranteed,” CNET wearables expert Vanessa Hand Orellana says. Less likely are a new Apple Watch SE and Ultra model since they were refreshed in 2025. But any new watches, the Series 12 and Ultra 4, are likely to come with a new processor, which should extend their life and usefulness for you.

The biggest design change expected is largely mechanical, not aesthetic. A more energy-efficient screen technology could be included to extend the watches’ battery life without sacrificing screen brightness. A new processor — probably named the S12 to match the line-up’s naming, despite “S11” being next in line — would also help with this.

The next Apple Watch Series 12 may bring back TouchID. 

Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

Another potential addition could be biometric authentication — in other words, a Touch ID for Apple Watch. Some internal code leaks suggest Apple is working on integrating this tech into its wearables, but it’s unclear when it will be publicly available. Health features, like blood pressure monitoring, are also rumored to be in progress, but again, no guarantees. The Apple Health App’s AI overhaul has also reportedly run into issues.

Our early testing shows WatchOS 27 with Siri AI will bring a big boost to devices — at least, for the ones it’s compatible with, which isn’t all of them. Watches were excluded from Apple’s summer price hike, but similar raises from watches by Google and Samsung mean a higher starting price isn’t out of the realm of possibility.

AirPods with or without cameras

Possibly the biggest Apple rumor has been that the next generation of Apple AirPods will be equipped with a new, tiny infrared camera — not to take photos, but to scan its physical environment to power its visual intelligence, or AI, answers. 

The AirPods 5 could look similar to the AirPods 4 (shown) but have performance upgrades.David Carnoy/CNET

These rumored “AirPods Ultra” sparked a lot of concern and outrage from tech enthusiasts, who have spent most of the summer criticizing other AI-and-camera-enabled wearables, like Meta’s smart glasses. Apple is known to tout its focus on privacy, so it will be interesting to see if Apple ultimately comes out with these earbuds and, if so, how it defends them.

AirPods are generally on a two-year refresh cycle, so we may get the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 Pro this year. The previous model, the AirPods 4 with active noise canceling, is “something of a technological marvel,” CNET headphones expert David Carnoy said. Effective noise canceling is hard to achieve with an open-earbud design, but Apple’s previous success sets the foundation for even more progress here. The Apple-owned Beats 360 headphones could also get refreshed this fall.

For more, check out the best iPhones and best MacBooks for 2026.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Katelyn Chedraoui

											Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators. Her work explores how new AI technology is infiltrating our lives, shaping the content we consume on social media and affecting the people behind the screens. Lenovo’s new 13-inch 3.5K Android tablet just hit a new all-time low at $332 for Labor Day

Alongside Amazon’s ongoing Labor Day sale, you’ll find Lenovo offering the Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 Android tablet for $332.49 shipped right now. Be sure to enter promo code EXTRAFIVE at checkout to see the discounted price. This is still a fairly new model that only debuted in July this year, and the 8GB/128GB configuration highlighted here normally carries a $500 price tag. That puts this deal at roughly $168 off, which lands it $47 below its previous all-time low. Today’s offer delivers a 34% discount and marks a new best price to beat for a relatively new and feature-packed Lenovo tablet. Head below for more details.

The Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 is one of the newer additions to Lenovo’s Android tablet lineup, and this particular model pairs Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 processor with 8GB of LPDDR5X memory and 128GB of UFS 3.1 storage. You also get a large 13-inch 3.5K display with a 3504 x 2190 resolution, offering plenty of room for schoolwork, streaming, reading, and multitasking. The rest of the hardware is solid too, with an 8MP front camera and face unlock, a quad-speaker JBL setup with Dolby Atmos, Wi-Fi 7, and Android 16 out of the box. It’s a pretty well-rounded option if you want a larger Android tablet with a sharper display and newer internals without stepping all the way up to Samsung’s more expensive flagship models.

title: Phil Schiller steps down from leading the App Store and Apple events
snippet: Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role leading the App Store and Apple events, according to a new Bloomberg report. The move is the latest progression of Schiller’s tenure at Apple, which spans multiple decades. more…
fullText:
Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role leading the App Store and Apple events, according to a new Bloomberg report. The move is the latest progression of Schiller’s tenure at Apple, which spans multiple decades.

Phil Schiller will remain an ‘Apple Fellow’ for now

Schiller was Apple’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing until 2020, when he transitioned into a new “Apple Fellow” role. Greg Joswiak took over the SVP marketing role at that point.

When Apple announced Schiller’s transition to Apple Fellow, it said he would continue to lead the App Store and Apple events. In 2024, The Wall Street Journal reported that Schiller was still working “nearly 80 hours a week.”

Despite stepping down as head of the App Store and Apple events, Schiller will remain an Apple Fellow and work on “unspecified initiatives.” Still, the report says that Apple employees believe this is a “big step” toward Schiller eventually retiring.

In conjunction with Schiller’s departure, Bloomberg reports that Apple is shifting leadership of the App Store to its services team led by Eddy Cue.

With the latest change, Apple is moving responsibility for the App Store over to the services division run by executive Eddy Cue. He previously oversaw the App Store until 2015, when that job was given to Schiller and the marketing department. Cue is taking on a more influential role under Ternus, Bloomberg has reported.

On a day-to-day basis, the App Store will be led by Carson Oliver, a veteran of the department who is now reporting directly to Cue. Two years ago, Schiller split up responsibility for the App Store among two direct reports, Oliver and Ann Thai.

Leadership of Apple events, meanwhile, is being handed to Nola Weinstein, who “has led that function as Schiller’s deputy since 2023.” Weinstein will report to Kristin Huguet Quayle, Apple’s VP of communications and public relations.

The big news of the day, of course, is that today marks Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO. John Ternus will take the keys on Tuesday. Cook commemorated his last day as CEO in a memo to Apple employees, which you can read here.
